interpretation: Each old and new case is one separate 15-second wall-clock observation, with different gameplay positions and frame counts.
Per-seat and range ratios are descriptive, not confidence intervals or an isolated per-frame rollback-cost measurement.
Original old/new observation, save and 100 ms results remain separate; no failed measurement is replaced.
The old first-run save flag remains false. Its separately named underlying-byte persistence result is retained from the pinned audit.
The comparison does not establish results on hardware GPUs, separate physical devices, phones, adaptive input delays or full campaigns.
Wasm linear-memory capacity contains the simulation heap and journal; these values must not be added to estimate process RSS.
Additional observer wall is reported separately. Shell and light in-callback hooks remain inside callback wall.

diagnosis.processCpuMeaning: Browser process CPU counters over about 16.17-second brackets including profiler start/stop; near-concurrent rates, not exact 15-second window rates or hardware GPU execution time.
diagnosis.textureMeaning: Zero uploads applies to these warmed measured battle windows, not all fonts, resource transitions or the full campaign.

coverage: Existing real native mp_tick, journaled game memory, native Update/Draw, full-resolution readback and independent pure-delay instance assertions.
First speculative clear_image changes actual game-owned pixels; backend.prepare and save_surfaces perform real upload and glReadPixels.
Replay samples independently reconstructed for every frame and seat, with structural and FNV validation.
evidenceLimits: Per-frame exact scalar traces and paired full-resolution equality are asserted by the SHA-verified browser driver; reports retain trajectory digests and selected snapshots, not both entire raw traces.
The fixture calls mp_tick directly and does not exercise BrowserRuntime rAF scheduling. Native scheduler tests and production browser performance validate that separate path.
Lifecycle requests exercise native stage/ending/results owners; authored story/staff-script completion and live ACK retirement are outside this fixture.

limitations: These are six optimized production observations, each measured once. Every original observation/save/performance flag is retained.
Previous results come from the SHA-256-pinned independent audit and hash-verified original observations, including its first save-observer signedness failure.
Diagnostic GL wrappers and CPU profiles are ineligible for performance acceptance and are rejected from the final matrix.
Old/new ratios are descriptive results from single fixed real-time windows, not replicated confidence intervals or identical-frame benchmarks.
Window submissions are default-framebuffer color blits, not GPU completion or monitor scanout.
Callback wall includes the production shell and lightweight hooks. Observer wall covers only post-callback status reads.
Different real-time modes reach different gameplay positions; cross-mode ratios are not isolated rollback overhead.
Console messages have timestamps but no URLs. Their cause remains unknown.
Parent runtime error events have no timestamps or call stacks; the first status sample supplies a bound, not exact onset.
No screenshots or framebuffer comparisons are made by this performance audit.
Native score/config file validation is the original Runtime result. This offline audit independently compares underlying bytes and hashes, without executing native validation again.

File byte/native-validation results and post-window Replay input proof are reported independently. The legacy underlying-byte save gate still includes every other original save requirement; it is not a file-integrity-only result.
A native-poll result of Completed is the time completion was observed; actual completion may precede that poll by up to the polling interval or scheduling delay.
Sparse save events reuse the previous rollback snapshot, with rollbackObservedAt. Those arrays are not asserted to describe the exact request or completion instant.
Overlap of a save interval with a long hold is temporal evidence, not proof that the save caused that hold.
The three-player pure-delay and zero-delay windows had long stalls. The outside-callback time has no CPU trace and is not attributed to one resource.
The original input proof failure is preserved: all 16 frames [758,774) exist, fire is set, right is absent. Life/ready was not recorded, so the exact gameplay cause is unresolved.
Current process inspections are post-run observations and cannot establish that no competing process existed inside historical windows.
All native Draws and GPU history submissions remain executed; render-target coverage and historical texture contracts would be needed for broader GPU coalescing.
